significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that information-matched lexicalization produces a "NAMED > DESCRIBED > EXEMPLIFIED ordering" whose advantage "grows with concept compositional depth," thereby predicting performance across depths, concept combinations, and re-skinned structural domains rather than merely asserting that labels encode concepts. This would establish a weighty behavioral phenomenon and a partial mechanism—label reuse as a compression scaffold—relevant to the language–thought question framed by Waxman and Markow's label-as-category work and Lupyan's label-feedback hypothesis, although the claimed trace correlation and stable representation do not by themselves fully distinguish compression from attentional anchoring. The negative branch is also informative and determinate: absence of the information-controlled ordering or depth interaction would rule out the specific claim that naming itself, rather than definitional content, scaffolds these reasoning tasks. Under topic substitution, the generic question of whether language affects AI intelligence would not earn this score; the claim-specific ordering and depth-dependent law are what place it above the topic-median correlational hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the intervention "a coined word plus one-line definition" used as a "reusable compression handle," together with the predicted compositional-depth interaction as a diagnostic of when lexical scaffolding should help. It is ex ante because labels can be introduced in prompts or curricula before structural reasoning occurs, giving prompt designers and model trainers an action window rather than merely explaining completed failures. After per-model recalibration, the conclusion would still predict the qualitative "NAMED > DESCRIBED" ordering and a widening advantage with depth across the asserted class of LLM structural tasks, though the claim's acknowledged focus on synthetic concepts limits confidence that the same rule governs naturalistic knowledge or non-language architectures. The topic-substitution check lowers no further: the broad language–intelligence topic alone supplies neither this intervention nor its depth-dependent transferable relation, while uptake plausibly extends from interpretability researchers to practitioners constructing prompts and curricula.
